Governing regulations for attendance, evaluation, grading and branch change eligibility —

1. Mandatory Attendance Requirement
1.1  Every student must maintain a minimum of 75% attendance in each registered course (theory, laboratory,
tutorial, and studio components counted separately) calculated cumulatively from the first working day of the
semester up to the last instructional day.
1.2  Attendance is recorded on a per-lecture / per-session basis through the Learning Management System
(LMS) and is visible to students in real time on the Student Portal under "My Attendance."
1.3  A student whose attendance falls below 75% in any course at the end of the semester is detained from
appearing in the End Semester Examination (ESE) for that course and is awarded a grade of "DT" (Detained)
on the grade card.
1.4  Students detained under Clause 1.3 must re-register for and repeat the course (along with attendance and
internal assessment) the next time it is offered.
1.5 Medical / Documented Exemption
A relaxation of up to 10% on the mandatory attendance requirement (i.e., a floor of 65%) may be granted by the
Dean of Academic Affairs on the recommendation of the Head of Department, only where all of the following
conditions are satisfied:

The absence is supported by a certificate from a registered medical practitioner or government hospital,
submitted within 7 working days of resuming classes.

The absence does not exceed 15 consecutive instructional days in a single spell, except in cases of
hospitalisation, which require the discharge summary as additional proof.

A duly filled Attendance Exemption Form (Form AA-04), countersigned by the parent/guardian and the class
coordinator, is submitted to the Department Office.

The exemption request is filed before the last teaching day of the semester; retrospective requests after
result declaration are not entertained.
Note: The 10% medical relaxation reduces the effective requirement to 65%; it does not waive attendance altogether.
Sports, NCC/NSS, and university-representation duty are covered under a separate Duty Leave provision (Clause 1.6)
and are recorded as "present" for attendance computation, subject to prior approval from the Dean of Student Welfare.
1.6 Duty Leave
Students representing the University in inter-university sports, technical festivals, cultural competitions,
NCC/NSS camps, or academic conferences (with a presented/accepted paper) may avail Duty Leave on
submission of Form AA-07 at least 3 working days in advance, endorsed by the concerned Dean/Director. Duty
Leave days are counted as present but are capped at 15 working days per semester per student.

2. Grading Scale
The University follows a 10-point Relative Grading System. Final grades in each course are computed from a
weighted combination of Continuous Internal Assessment (CIA) and the End Semester Examination, in the ratio
notified by the concerned School at the start of the semester (typically 40:60 for theory and 50:50 for lab-heavy
courses).

2.1  Cumulative Grade Point Average (CGPA) is computed as the credit-weighted average of grade points
across all courses completed up to the current semester. Semester Grade Point Average (SGPA) covers a
single semester only.
2.2  A minimum grade of "P" (Grade Point 4) is required to clear a course. A grade of "F" requires the student to
reappear in the ESE (backlog) in the immediately following exam cycle, or re-register for the full course if two
consecutive reappear attempts are unsuccessful.
2.3  Grade cards are issued through the Student Portal within 21 working days of the last ESE paper of the
semester. Physical grade cards are issued only at the end of the programme.
3. Branch Change Eligibility
Students seeking a change of branch/specialisation after the first year of the programme must satisfy all of the
following criteria:

Minimum CGPA of 8.50 at the end of the Second Semester, computed on all courses attempted (including
electives and audit courses carrying credit).

No active backlog — no course with grade "F" or "DT" pending clearance at the time of application.

Availability of a vacant seat in the target branch, subject to the sanctioned intake approved by the University
and applicable regulatory body for that academic year.

Submission of the Branch Change Application (Form AA-11) within the notified window, typically the first two
weeks of the Third Semester.
3.1  Where the number of eligible applicants for a target branch exceeds available seats, selection is made
strictly in order of CGPA, with ties resolved by the Second Semester SGPA, and thereafter by the First Semester
SGPA.

3.2  A branch change once granted and confirmed is final for the duration of the programme. Fee structure
applicable to the new branch (if different) takes effect from the semester of transfer; no retrospective fee
adjustment is made for prior semesters.
4. Unfair Means & Academic Integrity — Cross-Reference
Provisions relating to use of unfair means during examinations, plagiarism in assignments/reports, and
associated penalties are governed separately under the Examination Regulations document
(CU/ACAD/EXAM/2025-26); this document addresses attendance, grading and branch-change matters only.
This document is issued for general student guidance. In case of any conflict between this summary and the full
Academic Ordinances approved by the Academic Council, the version held by the Office of Academic Affairs shall
prevail. Queries: academics@chitkara.edu.in

1. Seating Arrangement
1.1  Seating for the End Semester Examination is allotted centrally by the Examination Cell and published on the
Student Portal and examination hall notice boards at least 3 days before the first paper.

Students are seated by roll number in a zig-zag / alternate pattern across rows, with a minimum gap of one
vacant seat on either side wherever hall capacity permits.

Where two examinations are held simultaneously in adjoining halls, different courses/subjects are interleaved
row-wise to minimise the possibility of copying between adjacent candidates.

A student must occupy only the seat number printed on their admit card; occupying another seat without
permission from the Room Superintendent is itself recorded as an irregularity.

Bags, books, notes, and mobile phones must be deposited at the front of the hall before the exam begins;
only admit card, ID card, and permitted stationery are allowed at the desk.
1.2  Entry to the examination hall closes 15 minutes after commencement of the paper; no candidate is
permitted entry thereafter, and no candidate is permitted to leave within the first 30 minutes or the last 10
minutes of the examination.
2. Use of Unfair Means (UFM)
2.1  "Unfair means" includes, without limitation: possession of unauthorised material (written notes, programmed
devices, mobile phones) in the examination hall; copying from another candidate or allowing one's own answer
script to be copied; impersonation; disorderly conduct towards invigilation staff; and any act calculated to secure
an unfair advantage in an examination or continuous assessment (including plagiarism in project
reports/assignments).
2.2  An invigilator detecting a suspected UFM case must seize the material/device, record a written report
co-signed by the candidate (or noting refusal to sign), and forward the answer script and evidence to the
Controller of Examinations the same day. The candidate is permitted to complete the remainder of the
examination under observation, without prejudice to the outcome of the enquiry.
2.3 Penalty Structure

2.4  All UFM cases are heard by the Unfair Means Committee, which affords the candidate an opportunity to be
heard before a penalty is confirmed. A candidate found using unfair means loses the right to "benefit of doubt"
grading and, for Category B and above, is also debarred from being considered for scholarships/merit awards for
the academic year in question.
2.5  A candidate may appeal the Committee's decision in writing to the Controller of Examinations within 7
working days of communication of the penalty; the appeal is placed before an Appellate Committee whose
decision is final.

--- Page 3 ---

3. Minimum Passing Marks
3.1  To clear a course, a candidate must secure:

A minimum of 40% aggregate marks (Continuous Internal Assessment + End Semester Examination
combined), corresponding to Grade "P" or above, and

A minimum of 30% marks in the End Semester Examination component alone, even where the combined
aggregate crosses 40% — a candidate scoring below this ESE floor is awarded grade "F" irrespective of
internal marks.

For laboratory/practical courses, a separate minimum of 40% in the practical/viva-voce component is
required in addition to the theory component, where the course carries both.
3.2  There is no separate minimum threshold within Continuous Internal Assessment alone; however, a
candidate scoring zero in CIA due to non-submission of assignments or non-appearance in a Mid-Term test is
not exempted from the ESE floor above.
3.3  Candidates who fail to meet the criteria in Clause 3.1 are classified as having grade "F" and must reappear
in the ESE for that course in the next available examination cycle (backlog/reappear), on payment of the
prescribed reappear fee.
4. Re-evaluation & Rechecking
4.1  A candidate may apply for rechecking (verification of totalling and ensuring all answers are evaluated) within
10 days of result declaration; revaluation (re-assessment by a second examiner) is permitted only for theory
papers, not for practicals, vivas, or CIA components, and is subject to the fee notified in the Fee Circular.
4.2  Where revaluation results in a change of 10% or more in the marks originally awarded, the revaluation fee is
refunded to the candidate.
This document summarises the Examination Regulations for general student awareness. The detailed Unfair Means
enquiry procedure and the full Examination Manual are maintained by the Examination Cell. Queries:
examcell@chitkara.edu.in

3. Scholarships
3.1  Merit and merit-cum-means scholarships are disbursed as a fee waiver credited directly against the tuition
ledger before the due date, provided eligibility documents (previous semester grade card, income certificate
where applicable) are uploaded on the Scholarship Portal by 15 February 2026.

Merit Scholarship: Students securing CGPA 9.0 and above in the preceding semester — up to 25% tuition
waiver, renewed automatically each semester subject to maintaining CGPA 8.5+.

Sports/Cultural Scholarship: State/National level achievers — waiver ranging 10%–50% as assessed by
the Sports Committee, valid for the academic year.

Means-cum-Merit Scholarship: Family income below ■6,00,000 p.a. with CGPA 7.5+ — waiver assessed
case-by-case by the Financial Aid Committee.

Sibling/Alumni Concession: 10% concession on tuition where a sibling is concurrently enrolled, or the
applicant is a child of a Chitkara University alumnus (proof required).
3.2  Scholarships are not cumulative beyond a combined ceiling of 50% of tuition fee unless specifically
approved by the Vice-Chancellor's office. A scholarship is forfeited for the following semester if the student
incurs a backlog ("F" grade) or a disciplinary sanction.

1.1  The standard in-time (curfew) for general UG residents from the Third Year onward is 9:30 PM on
working days, recorded via biometric attendance at the hostel main gate. First and second year residents
observe an earlier in-time of 8:30 PM in line with the Anti-Ragging and student-safety protocol for new entrants.
1.2  Three unexplained late entries in a semester result in a written warning; a fourth instance is referred to the
Hostel Disciplinary Committee and may attract a fine of ■500 per instance thereafter or a period of early curfew
(7:30 PM) for the remainder of the semester.
1.3  Overnight leave (Out-Pass) beyond curfew requires prior written consent from a parent/guardian submitted
through the Hostel Portal at least 12 hours in advance, and is capped at 4 occasions per month.
2. Anti-Ragging Policy
2.1  Chitkara University maintains a strict zero-tolerance policy on ragging in accordance with UGC
Regulations, 2009 and applicable state Anti-Ragging Acts, across hostel premises, mess halls, common rooms,
and campus grounds.

All fresh entrants and their parents/guardians must submit a signed Anti-Ragging Affidavit (online, via the
UGC Anti-Ragging portal and the University portal) before hostel allotment.

Anti-Ragging Squads conduct surprise checks in hostel corridors, mess, and common areas, particularly
during the first 90 days of an academic year.

A 24x7 Anti-Ragging Helpline and a designated Anti-Ragging Committee (chaired by the Dean, Student
Welfare) are constituted to receive and act on complaints confidentially.

Confirmed incidents of ragging attract penalties ranging from a written apology and fine, up to rustication,
expulsion from the hostel, debarment from examinations, or expulsion from the University, as per the severity
assessed by the Committee, without prejudice to criminal proceedings under law.
2.2  Any student witnessing or experiencing ragging is encouraged to report immediately to the Warden-on-Duty,
the Anti-Ragging Helpline, or anonymously through the drop-box installed in each hostel block. Retaliation
against a complainant is treated as a separate, aggravated offence.

3.1  Visitors (parents/guardians and University-approved guests) are permitted only in the designated Visitors'
Lounge at the hostel entrance, between 10:00 AM and 6:00 PM on all days; visitors are not permitted inside
residential wings under any circumstance.
3.2  Every visitor must register at the security gate with a valid photo ID; the resident student is intimated and
must personally receive the visitor at the lounge.
3.3  Opposite-gender visitors, including family members, are restricted to the Visitors' Lounge only and are not
permitted in the hostel premises beyond the reception/lounge area at any time.
3.4  Overnight stay of guests inside student rooms is strictly prohibited. Parents requiring overnight
accommodation may be directed to the University Guest House, subject to availability and prior booking.
